question_or_symptom: A deterministic simulated virtual address can look like a packet-executable GPU virtual address even when the bridge only owns a functional byte store.
observation: The current bridge has no packet processor, GPU page-table binding, or shader-visible memory path. An allocation slot and arithmetic address formula establish stable host-protocol identity, not execution visibility.
conclusion: Functional allocation identity and packet-executable GPU VA are separate claims that must not be collapsed.
decision: Key every functional allocation by client file descriptor, client generation, allocation slot, and allocation generation; derive one deterministic functional VA per slot; reject stale ownership; and explicitly withhold packet-visible VRAM or execution claims until a later page-table and dispatch gate proves them.
invalidated_assumptions: A stable numeric virtual address is sufficient evidence that GPU packets can dereference it.
An allocation ID alone remains unique after disconnect or slot reuse.
